facts.value:
A pure Go PDF library — no CGo, no native libraries, no third-party package dependencies
(standard library only), MIT-licensed. It creates, edits, renders, signs, encrypts, converts, and
validates PDF documents: split/merge/extract pages, extract and search text, fill and build
AcroForms, draw text/vector graphics/tables, embed and subset fonts, apply digital signatures
(PKCS#7, PAdES, timestamps), validate and convert PDF/A, author accessible Tagged PDF, and
render pages to images with a built-in rasterizer that has no third-party package dependencies of
its own, convert to and from Markdown, HTML, and SVG, and query documents through a set of AI
copilots over any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

facts.value:
- **Page-level operations and metadata** — `Document.Split()` breaks a document into per-page
  documents; `Extract` builds a new document from selected `PageRange`s without touching the
  source; `Append` combines multiple PDFs into one by merging another document's pages in place;
  `Rotate`/`SetRotation` turn pages, and `Reorder` rearranges them by an explicit 1-based index
  slice (repeats and omissions both allowed); `Document.NUp`/`Document.Booklet` (`NUp`/`Booklet`)
  impose pages onto larger sheets for N-up printing or saddle-stitch binding, each returning a new
  document built from Form XObjects and leaving the source untouched; and blank PDFs can be
  created from scratch with `NewDocument`/`NewDocumentFromFormat`. Each `*Page` exposes its own
  `Number()`, `Size()` (a `PageSize{Width, Height}` in points), and `Rotation()` getters, and page
  geometry (`MediaBox`/`CropBox`/`TrimBox`/`BleedBox`/`ArtBox`) is readable and, via
  `SetMediaBox`/`SetCropBox`/`SetTrimBox`/`SetBleedBox`/`SetArtBox` (plus the `SetPageSize`
  shorthand for resizing the MediaBox), writable without scaling existing content —
  `Document.ResizeContents` (`ResizePage`, `ResizeMargins`, `ResizeContentSize`, …) rescales the
  content with the page instead, annotations included; the `/Info`
  dictionary round-trips through `Document.Info()`/`SetInfo()`/`ClearInfo()` and a `DocumentInfo`
  struct, distinct from the XMP metadata packet available via
  `Document.XMP()`/`SetXMP()`/`ClearXMP()` (backed by the `/Catalog/Metadata` stream, with a raw
  `XMPRaw()`/`SetXMPRaw()` escape hatch and `SyncInfoToXMP()` to mirror `/Info` into XMP); and the
  `/PageLabels` numbering tree is written with `Document.SetPageLabels` (roman/decimal/alphabetic
  styles, prefix, and start value per range) and read back per-page via `Page.Label()`.
  `Document.Version()`/`SetVersion()` read and choose the PDF version (saving never lowers it),
  `Document.ConvertToPDF20()` turns a document into PDF 2.0 (metadata moved into XMP, what PDF 2.0
  deprecates removed; RC4 or AES-128 encryption is refused with `ErrDeprecatedFeature`), and
  `Document.ID()` returns the file identifier as a `DocumentID{Original, Modified}`;
  `Document.PageMode()`/`SetPageMode()` choose the panel a viewer opens with (bookmarks,
  thumbnails, layers, attachments, or full screen), and `Page.SetTransition`/`SetDisplayDuration`
  give a page its presentation-mode transition (`PageTransition`) and auto-advance time.
- **Encryption and digital signatures** — `Document.SetPassword(userPassword, ownerPassword)`
  password-protects the document on save with AES-128 (`/CFM /AESV2`), AES-256 (`/CFM /AESV3`,
  bumps the file to PDF 2.0), or RC4-128 and granular viewer permissions (print, copy, modify,
  annotate, fill, accessibility, assemble); sign with a PKCS#7-detached signature
  (SHA-256, RSA or ECDSA) that can be PAdES, a DocMDP certification, and/or carry an RFC 3161
  trusted timestamp, over plain or already-encrypted documents, with support for multiple
  incremental signatures and verification via `VerifySignatures` — optionally asking the issuer
  whether the signing certificate was revoked (OCSP or CRL, network opt-in through
  `ValidationOptions`) and embedding that evidence as a `/DSS` with `AddValidationInfo`, so the
  signature still verifies after the certificate expires (LTV). Keys are passed as a standard
  `crypto.Signer` plus `*x509.Certificate` — no `.p12` file required. Documents can also be
  encrypted for **certificate recipients** instead of a password
  (`EncryptionOptions.Recipients`, the `/Adobe.PubSec` handler): each recipient gets its own
  permissions, and the file opens with `OpenWithCertificate(path, cert, key)` for any
  `crypto.Decrypter`.
- **Content authoring with the Flow layout engine** — `Document.NewFlow` lays out paragraphs,
  headings, images, tables, and lists top-to-bottom with automatic pagination; floating boxes
  (absolute, in-flow, or floated with text wrap-around) and multi-column layout are built on the
  same engine; `FlowOptions.Tagged` auto-tags every element for a one-call PDF/UA-conformant
  document.
- **Tables and vector graphics** — `pdf.NewTable()` builds multi-page tables with repeating
  header rows (auto-fit or explicit `Row.SetHeight`), cell merging via
  `Cell.SetColSpan`/`SetRowSpan`, per-cell styling, and image cells via `Cell.SetImage`, rendered
  onto a page with `(*Page).AddTable(t, rect)`; `(*Page).DrawLine`/`DrawRectangle`/`DrawCircle`/
  `DrawPath` and friends draw first-class vector content directly on a page, and a `Path` fluent
  builder (`MoveTo`/`LineTo`/`CurveTo`/`QuadTo`/`Arc`/`Close`) covers arbitrary shapes; fills
  support solid colours, `ShapeStyle.FillGradient` (linear or radial), and
  `Document.CreateTilingPattern(w, h)` repeating-motif tiling patterns.
- **AcroForms** — read, and build from scratch every standard field type with
  `AddTextField`/`AddCheckbox`/`AddRadioGroup`/`AddComboBox`/`AddListBox`/`AddPushButton` (plus
  the typed password/file-select/rich-text/number/date variants — behavior flags exposed as `/Ff`
  on the underlying field dictionary) and remove one with `RemoveField`; `AddBarcodeField` draws
  Code128, QR, or PDF417 symbols in place of text, encoded by this library's own pure-Go encoders (no
  external dependency); `Field.SetStyle`/`Style()` control widget appearance (border, background, font),
  and `(*ButtonField).SetAppearance` gives push buttons distinct normal/rollover/down captions
  and an icon; field values round-trip as typed JSON, FDF, and XFDF for template-fill and
  Acrobat-interoperable data interchange.
- **Annotations, bookmarks, and redaction** — the full ISO 32000-1 markup/drawing annotation
  family with auto-regenerated appearance streams, hierarchical outlines (`OutlineItemCollection`)
  and named destinations with all 8 PDF destination types, and mark-then-apply redaction that
  irreversibly removes text, images, and paths from the marked regions. `Document.Flatten()`/
  `Form.Flatten()` bake interactive fields and annotations into static page content so the
  result renders identically but is no longer editable.
  Printer's marks (trim, bleed, registration, colour bars, page information) go in the margin
  outside the TrimBox, one by one or with `AddPrinterMarks`.
- **Attachments and portfolios** — `Document.EmbeddedFiles()` attaches, reads back, and removes
  document-level files through the `/Catalog/Names/EmbeddedFiles` name tree, while
  `Document.Collection()` turns those attachments into a **PDF portfolio**: a schema of custom
  columns (`Schema().Add("Amount", "Total", CollectionFieldNumber)`), per-file values via
  `EmbeddedFile.CollectionItem()`, an initial file, a sort order, and a details/tiles/hidden
  presentation mode — so viewers show a navigable table instead of a plain attachment list, and
  the cover page still opens anywhere.
- **Tagged PDF and PDF/UA accessibility** — `Document.TaggedContent()` builds a logical structure
  tree as content is drawn (`TagContent`, `AddTaggedTable`, `AddTaggedList`), links and other
  annotations join the tree via `StructElement.AddObjectReference` (an `/OBJR` to the annotation
  itself, not marked content), `Document.AutoTag()` tags a PDF made elsewhere after the fact
  (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, figures in reading order; headers, footers and drawings
  as artifacts) without changing how it looks, `Document.ConvertToPDFUA()` embeds the fonts and
  writes the PDF/UA identifier, and `Document.ValidatePDFUA()` reports what is still missing.

facts.value:
- **PDF/A and structural validation** — `Validate` checks structural integrity;
  `ValidatePDFA(PDFA1B/2B/3B/1A/2A/3A/2U/3U/4/4E/4F)` reports archival-conformance violations; `ConvertToPDFA`
  moves a document toward conformance in one call (strips encryption/JavaScript, embeds
  non-embedded Standard-14 fonts, adds an sRGB ICC OutputIntent, writes the `pdfaid` XMP packet). For
  PDF/A-1, pages that really paint with transparency become images with their text kept as an invisible,
  searchable layer; the report's `RasterizedPages` names them. `ConvertDeviceCMYKToRGB` recolours
  DeviceCMYK first for documents that must conform under that sRGB intent.
- **E-invoices (ZUGFeRD / Factur-X)** — `Document.AttachInvoice(xml)` turns a document into a hybrid
  e-invoice: the CII XML is embedded as `factur-x.xml` with the associated-file relationship its
  profile calls for, the Factur-X metadata and extension schema are written, and the document is
  converted to PDF/A-3. `Document.Invoice()` extracts the invoice from incoming Factur-X and ZUGFeRD
  2.x/1.0 files together with its profile. Attachments also gain PDF/A-3 associated-file
  relationships (`EmbeddedFile.SetAFRelationship`).
- **Rendering to raster images** — a pure-Go anti-aliased renderer with no third-party package
  dependencies of its own (its own rasterizer — no `golang.org/x/image`, no cgo) draws vector
  graphics, images (including CCITT fax, JBIG2, and JPEG2000 (`/JPXDecode`) scans), and text
  (embedded and non-embedded via a `FontRepository` covering `.ttc`/`.otf` faces, including
  non-embedded CJK) to PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, and single- or multi-page
  TIFF via `Page.RenderImage`/`RenderPNG`/`RenderTIFF`/… and `Document.RenderTIFF`.
- **HTML, SVG, and Markdown conversion** — `SaveHTML` exports a single-file HTML document with no
  external assets in four modes (faithful raster, visible text, native SVG-per-page, and
  reflowable), including fillable AcroForm controls; in text/native modes, embedded TrueType/
  OpenType fonts are re-wrapped as WOFF `@font-face` data URLs with a browser cmap synthesized
  from the font's `/ToUnicode` mapping, so text renders in the document's real faces. `SaveSVG`
  exports standalone true-vector SVG pages with all binary parts embedded as `data:` URLs by
  default, or externalized via `ResourceWriter`, and `AddSVG` imports SVG 1.1 content (shapes,
  gradients, clipping, masks) back onto a page; `MarkdownToDocument` renders CommonMark + GFM as a
  paginated PDF (652/652 on the official test suite), `Flow.AddMarkdown` mixes Markdown into a
  Flow document, `Page.AddMarkdown(md, rect)` draws it into a `Rectangle` on an existing page, and
  `SaveMarkdown` re-assembles a PDF as GFM Markdown.
- **Stamps and watermarks** — `Document.AddTextWatermark`/`AddSVGWatermark` overlay a text or SVG
  watermark across selected pages (or every page); `(*Page).AddStamp`/`(*Document).AddStamp` place
  a `TextStamp`, `ImageStamp`, or `PageNumberStamp` on one or more pages.
- **Table detection and Office/eBook conversion** — `TableAbsorber` (`Visit(page)` then
  `TableList()`) recognizes ruled and borderless tables directly from a page's vector geometry (no
  rasterization), with conservative guards so ordinary prose, lists, TOCs, and code listings are
  never mistaken for tables; `Remove` and `Replace` delete a found table or draw a new `Table` in
  its place. Detection feeds `Document.SaveDocx`/`WriteDocx` (a pure-stdlib OOXML
  writer producing styled runs, heading styles, hyperlinks, and lists, plus real Word tables —
  `EnhancedFlow`, the default mode — from detected table structure), `Document.SaveXlsx`/
  `WriteXlsx` (detected tables become Excel worksheets with real numeric cells, merged cells, and
  header shading, or a full-page cell-per-line mode), and `Document.SaveEpub`/`WriteEpub` (a
  reflowable, spec-correct OCF-container EPUB 3 book with chapters split at headings and a real
  navigation TOC).
- **Document comparison** — `CompareDocumentsPageByPage` and `CompareFlatDocuments` report what
  changed between two PDFs word by word, with the page and rectangle of every difference;
  `ComparisonResult.SaveMarkup` writes a copy of either document in which insertions are
  highlighted, deletions struck out and removed text kept in the annotation note, so a reviewer
  reads the change list in any PDF viewer. `GraphicalPdfComparer.GetDifference` catches what the
  word comparer can't — moved or edited graphics, font substitution — by rasterizing both pages and
  diffing pixels, reporting a changed-pixel ratio and a difference image; `SideBySideComparePages`/
  `SideBySideCompareDocuments` lay the marked-up before/after side by side in one vector spread PDF.
  `HTMLDiffOutputGenerator`/`JSONDiffOutputGenerator`/`MarkdownDiffOutputGenerator`/
  `PDFDiffOutputGenerator` serialize the same differences as an HTML fragment, JSON, GFM Markdown, or
  a generated, colored PDF report. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `TextPdfComparer`,
  `GraphicalPdfComparer`, `SideBySidePdfComparer` and the `Aspose.Pdf.Comparison.OutputGenerator`
  namespace.
- **AI copilots** — the `ai` subpackage adds document summarization (`SummaryCopilot`), OCR of
  scanned pages with a `MakeSearchable` pipeline that writes recognized text back as an invisible,
  selectable layer, document Q&A with conversation history (`ChatCopilot`), and automatic
  `/Alt` text generation for tagged figures (`ImageDescriptionCopilot`), over any
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

facts.value:
- **Text object model** — the Aspose.PDF for .NET way to write and edit text: `TextBuilder.AppendText`
  draws a `TextFragment` of styled `TextSegment`s (`TextState`: font, size, colours, spacing,
  scaling, hyperlinks, backgrounds), `AppendParagraph` wraps, aligns and justifies a `TextParagraph`,
  and `TextFragmentAbsorber` finds text as editable fragments — set `Text`, `Position` or
  `TextState` and the page changes when the document is saved (or at once with `ApplyTextChanges`;
  a later search, and any operation that rewrites page content, applies it first).
- **Incremental save** — `SaveIncremental`/`WriteIncremental` keep the opened file's bytes and
  append only what changed as a new revision, so existing signatures stay valid.
- **Text extraction, fonts, and optimization** — extract text in visual or raw reading order
  (`TextExtractOptions{Mode: TextExtractRaw}`) with full layout info, limited to the page or a
  rectangle glyph by glyph (`LimitToPageBounds`, `Rectangle`), recover paragraph/column
  structure (`Paragraphs()`, optionally joining paragraphs that run on into the next column or page) and rewrite a paragraph in place (`MarkupParagraph.SetText`), re-align the text already in a
  rectangle — left, right, centred, justified — keeping its fonts (`TextParagraphAbsorber`), search and replace text in place, embed and subset TrueType/
  OpenType fonts (`.ttf`/`.otf`/`.ttc`) — `Document.LoadFont`/`Document.LoadFontByName("Calibri",
  bold, italic)` resolve faces by family name via a pluggable `FontRepository`, and
  `Document.SubsetFonts()` rebuilds each embedded font's own glyph tables (`glyf`/`loca`/`hmtx`/
  `CIDToGIDMap`) down to only the glyphs actually used; custom glyphs can also be authored
  outright with `Document.CreateType3Font()` — `Type3Font.AddGlyph(rune, width)` hands back a
  drawing canvas in glyph space, so a symbol drawn with the vector API becomes a real font
  character whose text still extracts and searches (an embedded `ToUnicode` CMap carries the
  mapping); `Document.RemoveUnusedObjects()` deletes
  every object that neither a page nor the document catalog uses (metadata, bookmarks,
  attachments and the structure tree are kept) and returns the removed count on its own, or fold that
  same cleanup into a larger pass with the unified `Document.Optimize` pass
  (`DefaultOptimizationOptions()` is the safe, lossless preset — remove unused objects, subset
  fonts, Flate-compress and dedupe streams, pack objects into object streams; opt into lossy image
  recompression via `OptimizationOptions.Images`, or into dropping a Helvetica/Times/Courier font's
  own embedded program via `OptimizationOptions.UnembedFonts`) or the image-only
  `Document.OptimizeImages(OptimizeImageOptions)`
  pass (max DPI downscaling, JPEG quality, and PNG→JPEG conversion); reduce file size further with
  `Document.SaveLinearized`/`WriteToLinearized` (linearized/fast-web-view output per ISO 32000-1
  Annex F, so viewers can render page 1 before the whole file downloads; `IsLinearized` tells whether
  an opened file is), or `ConvertToGrayscale`.

real before/after renders, all four stamp types, a word-level document comparison, the full
annotation gallery, redactions, multi-page tables, vector graphics, and a meta "Rendering & Imposition"
page whose thumbnails are renders of the document itself, produced by this library's own renderer.
Cross-cutting metadata — bookmarks, named destinations, page labels, and Info + XMP
metadata — is set once and carried through the whole document. The showcase itself is
deliberately left unencrypted so it previews inline on GitHub and opens in every viewer;
encryption (RC4 / AES-128 / AES-256) is covered in
[Encryption and Signing](#encryption-and-signing) below. Regenerate it locally with
`go run ./_examples/feature_showcase`.

evidence.detail: lines 476-483; paragraph; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference

facts.value:
The public API lives in the single root package `asposepdf` (imported as `pdf`), centered on
`Document` — opened via `Open`/`OpenStream`/`OpenWithPassword`/`OpenStreamWithPassword` (the
stream forms take any `io.Reader`) and serialized via `Document.WriteTo` (implements
`io.WriterTo`, so it writes to any `io.Writer`); its `Pages()` method returns live `*Page` views,
and nearly every mutating method (rotation, reorder, metadata, passwords, …) modifies the
receiver in place; `Split` and `Extract` are the two exceptions, each returning a fresh, fully
independent `*Document`. AI copilots live in the separate `ai` subpackage so the root package
stays free of network code.

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Encryption and Signing

evidence.detail: lines 756-776; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Encryption and Signing

facts.value:
- `Permissions` fields map to ISO 32000-1 §7.6.3.2 Table 22 bits 3–12; the library encodes them
  with the Adobe convention (reserved bits set high). In `EncryptionOptions`, `Permissions` is a
  pointer so `nil` means "grant all", distinguishing that default from an explicit
  `&Permissions{}`, which denies everything.
- `OpenWithPassword` reads Standard-handler files encrypted with RC4-40 (R2), RC4 (R3),
  AES-128 (R4, `/AESV2`) and AES-256 in both revision 6 and Acrobat 9's revision 5, and returns
  `ErrInvalidPassword` when the password matches neither the user nor the owner password.
  Writing always uses revision 6 for AES-256.
- `EncryptionOptions.Recipients` switches to the public-key security handler (ISO 32000-1
  §7.6.4): the document is sealed for a list of X.509 certificates — each with optional
  per-recipient `Permissions`, which a password cannot express — and opened with
  `OpenWithCertificate`/`OpenStreamWithCertificate` by supplying the certificate and any
  `crypto.Decrypter` private key. AES-128 (the default, as for a password) and AES-256 are supported; RSA
  recipients only, and the file re-saves for the same recipients after editing.
- `Document.Sign` covers the whole file with one PKCS#7-detached signature, invisible by default
  or visible via `Visible`/`Rect`/`Page`/`SignatureAppearance`; `PAdES` switches the subfilter to
  `ETSI.CAdES.detached`, `Certify` adds a DocMDP certification, and `TimestampURL` embeds an RFC
  3161 timestamp. Re-signing an already-signed document appends an incremental update so the
  earlier signature stays valid. `Document.VerifySignatures` returns `Valid`, `IntegrityOK`,
  `CoversWholeDocument`, and the signer `Certificate` per signature field — trust-chain validation
  against your own store is the caller's responsibility.

  as new page(s) at the front; `Page.AddTOC` renders a caller-supplied entry list into a

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Attachments and Portfolios

evidence.detail: lines 809-824; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Attachments and Portfolios

facts.value:
- `Document.EmbeddedFiles()` manages document-level attachments through the
  `/Catalog/Names/EmbeddedFiles` name tree (ISO 32000-1 §7.11.4): `Add(path)`/
  `AddFromStream(name, r)` embed a file (MIME type detected from the extension), and each
  `*EmbeddedFile` exposes `Name()`, `Description()`/`SetDescription()`, `MIMEType()`, `Size()`,
  and `Data()`/`WriteTo(w)`/`Save(path)` to read it back. The page-pinned counterpart is
  `FileAttachmentAnnotation`.
- `Document.Collection()` presents those attachments as a **portfolio** (ISO 32000-1 §7.11.6 and
  §12.3.5): `SetView(CollectionViewDetails|Tiles|Hidden)` chooses the presentation mode,
  `Schema().Add(key, header, type)` declares the columns a viewer shows — text, number, and date
  columns carry per-file values, while `CollectionFieldFilename`/`Description`/`ModDate`/
  `CreationDate`/`Size` are derived from the attachment itself (`CollectionField.IsDerived()`) — and `SetInitialFile(name)` plus
  `SetSort(field, ascending)` control what opens first and how the list is ordered. Values are
  written per attachment with `EmbeddedFile.CollectionItem()`
  (`SetText`/`SetNumber`/`SetDate`, read back with `Text`/`Number`/`Date`). `IsPortfolio()`
  reports the state and `Remove()` reverts the document to a plain attachment list without
  touching the files. Folder hierarchies (`/Folders`) are out of scope.

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Document JavaScript and Open Actions

evidence.detail: lines 828-840; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Document JavaScript and Open Actions

facts.value:
- `Document.JavaScript()` returns the document-level named-script collection, backed by the
  `/Catalog/Names/JavaScript` name tree (ISO 32000-1 §7.7.4 / §8.5.1) — `Add(name, script)`,
  `Get(name)`, `Has(name)`, `Remove(name)`, `Names()`, `Count()`, and `Clear()` manage it
  directly. This is distinct from the action-level `JavaScriptAction` that fires on an
  annotation click, not on the document-open event.
- `Document.OpenAction()`/`Document.SetOpenAction(act)`/`Document.RemoveOpenAction()` read, set,
  and clear the `/Catalog/OpenAction` entry (ISO 32000-1 §12.3.2 / §12.6.1) — the action a viewer
  runs when the document opens (GoTo, JavaScript, Named, …). A `GoTo` open action is bound to the
  document, so its destination resolves to a 1-based page number on read;
  `NewGoToDestinationAction(dest)` takes any of the eight explicit destination kinds or a
  `NamedDestination`, read back through `GoToAction.Destination()`; both round-trip through
  `Save` and coexist with named destinations. Document-level JavaScript executes in the
  recipient's viewer when the file is opened — embed only scripts you authored or audited.

facts.value:
- `Document.DeletePages(pageNums ...int)` removes one or more 1-based pages in place — page
  numbers are de-duplicated and validated before anything is removed, so a call that would remove
  every page returns an error and leaves the document unchanged; `Document.DeletePage(n)` is the
  single-page convenience form.

  page to the end of an already-open document; `Document.InsertBlankPage(position, width,
  height)`/`Document.InsertBlankPageFromFormat(position, format)` insert one at a specific
  1-based position instead — distinct from building a whole new document from scratch via
  `NewFlow`.

facts.value: ### Text Drawing and Right-to-Left / Arabic Shaping

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Text Drawing and Right-to-Left / Arabic Shaping

evidence.detail: lines 856-878; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Text Drawing and Right-to-Left / Arabic Shaping

facts.value:
- `TextStyle.RTL` (or simply including RTL characters) enables right-to-left/bidirectional layout
  for drawn text: a pure-Go Unicode Bidi Algorithm (UAX #9) implementation reorders each line
  into visual order, keeping embedded numbers and Latin runs left-to-right, and RTL paragraphs
  right-align by default. Arabic contextual shaping (connected letterforms plus lam-alef
  ligatures via Presentation Forms-B) renders proper Arabic with any font that covers the block,
  including the bundled DejaVu Sans.
- Embedded OpenType fonts are shaped by their own GSUB/GPOS tables: a pure-Go shaping engine
  applies contextual forms, ligatures, kerning, and cursive and mark attachment the way HarfBuzz
  does, glyph for glyph, so Arabic, Persian, and Urdu join in fonts without Presentation Forms-B
  (Amiri, Noto Naskh Arabic), vowel marks sit on their base letters, and Latin text kerns. It
  needs no API change — `AddText` shapes automatically — and shaped text stays extractable and
  searchable through `ToUnicode` mappings and `ActualText` spans.
- `AddText` wraps at white space but never at a no-break space (U+00A0, U+202F, U+2007), starts a
  new line at CR, LF, CRLF, NEL, U+2028 and U+2029, and breaks a word too long for the line after a
  hyphen or at a soft hyphen (drawn as a hyphen there) before cutting it elsewhere. Invisible
  characters (zero-width space, joiners, soft hyphens not used as a break) draw nothing with every
  font, and `TextStyle.MissingGlyph` reports, or replaces, exactly the characters a font cannot show.
- `Document.CreateType3Font()` authors a Type3 font (ISO 32000-1 §9.6.5), whose glyphs are
  content streams rather than outlines: `AddGlyph(r, width)` returns a `*Page` canvas in glyph
  space (1000 units per em, baseline at `y = 0`) that accepts the whole drawing API, and the
  finished font drops into `TextStyle.Font` alongside Standard-14 and embedded faces. The font
  freezes on first use, embedding each glyph as a `/CharProcs` stream plus a generated
  `ToUnicode` CMap, so text drawn with custom symbols still extracts, searches, and renders.

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Validation: Structural, PDF/A, and PDF/UA

evidence.detail: lines 922-953; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Validation: Structural, PDF/A, and PDF/UA

facts.value:
- `Validate` is a structural-integrity check only (`INVALID_HEADER`/`XREF_ERROR`/`OBJECT_ERROR`/
  `PAGE_TREE_ERROR`/`STREAM_ERROR`/`ENCRYPTED` issue codes) — not a PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance
  check.
- `ValidatePDFA(PDFA1B/2B/3B/1A/2A/3A/2U/3U/4/4E/4F)` inspects the XMP `pdfaid` identifier and undeclared XMP
  properties, font embedding and `/CIDSet`, encryption, forbidden actions, the ICC OutputIntent
  against device colour, transparency and layers (PDF/A-1), image interpolation, XFA, annotation
  flags and appearances, and metadata compression, and reads the embedded font programs for widths
  that disagree with the font dictionary, glyphs they do not define, and `.notdef`; the "a" levels
  additionally require a Tagged PDF (structure tree + `/Lang`).
- `ConvertToPDFA` strips encryption and forbidden actions, removes embedded files and flattens
  transparency for PDF/A-1, sets annotation print flags and draws the appearances annotations are
  missing, turns off image interpolation, removes XFA and transfer functions, embeds the fonts the
  document actually draws with — Standard-14 and other simple fonts through bundled
  metric-compatible clones, composite (CJK) fonts as a subset of the matching installed face, and
  Symbol or ZapfDingbats from a face registered through `AddFontFile`/`AddFontFolder` — adds a
  pure-Go sRGB ICC OutputIntent, and writes a `pdfaid` XMP packet that agrees with `/Info`, then
  returns a report of whatever still fails. DeviceCMYK content is not converted and is reported;
  `ConvertDeviceCMYKToRGB`, called first, recolours it the way the renderer shows it, at the cost of
  the CMYK values, and leaves ICCBased CMYK alone.
  The report covers the rules this library knows about, not every rule of the standard: on a
  sample of 337 real-world documents, 291 pass veraPDF as PDF/A-2b and 287 as PDF/A-1b, and the
  report accepts none that veraPDF rejects. Another document can still differ, so confirm
  conformance with veraPDF when it matters.
- PDF/A-4 (`PDFA4`, `PDFA4E`, `PDFA4F`) is written as a PDF 2.0 file. `/Info` is forbidden there, so
  `ConvertToPDFA` moves its contents to XMP and `Info()` comes back empty. JavaScript and field
  actions stay, as this part allows them. `PDFA4` requires any attachment to be PDF/A-1, 2 or 4 itself;
  `PDFA4F` takes any file and requires at least one; only `PDFA4F` allows file-attachment annotations.
- `ValidatePDFUA` checks the PDF/UA-1 (ISO 14289-1) requirements a program can decide: a Tagged PDF
  with `/StructTreeRoot` + `/ParentTree`, a declared `/Lang`, the `pdfuaid` identifier, a displayed
  XMP title, embedded fonts, alternate text on every figure/formula, `/Scope` on every `/TH`,
  headings in order, and accessibility not blocked by encryption. `ConvertToPDFUA` repairs what can
  be repaired without knowing the content; a file may be both PDF/A and PDF/UA.

attributes.section: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Tagged PDF Authoring

evidence.detail: lines 957-972; list; under Aspose.PDF FOSS for Go > API Reference > Tagged PDF Authoring

facts.value:
- `AddTaggedTable` renders a `Table` and builds its `/Table → /TR → /TH`/`/TD` structure in one
  call (repeating header rows become `/TH`); `AddTaggedList` does the same for bulleted/numbered
  lists. Decoration (headers, footers, page numbers) is marked as an artifact so it stays out of
  the structure tree.
- `StructElement.AddObjectReference` associates a structure element directly with an annotation via
  an `/OBJR` (ISO 32000-1 §14.7.4.4) instead of marked content — the way a `/Link` element points at
  its `LinkAnnotation` — and composes with `AddChild`/`TagContent` rather than replacing them.
- `Document.AutoTag(AutoTaggingSettings)` tags a document that has no structure tree: text is
  grouped into headings, paragraphs, lists and tables (with header rows and cell spans) in reading
  order, images become figures, and repeating headers/footers, watermarks and drawn graphics are
  marked as artifacts. Headings come from the bookmarks or from font sizes
  (`HeadingRecognitionStrategy`, as in Aspose.PDF for .NET). Only marked-content operators are
  inserted, so pages render and extract exactly as before. Figures carry no alternate text —
  `ImageDescriptionCopilot.FillAltTexts` writes it. Links, form fields and other annotations join
  the tree too. Follow with `ConvertToPDFUA()` for PDF/UA-1, `ConvertToPDFA(PDFA2A)` for an
  accessible archive, or both.

- `SaveSVG`/`WriteSVG` export standalone true-vector SVG with real Bézier paths, native strokes,
  and glyph-outline text (no font dependencies); `SVGSaveOptions.DPI` (default 150) sets the
  resolution of the small raster patches used only where shadings/patterns/soft masks can't be
  expressed in SVG.
- `MarkdownToDocument`/`FromStream` render headings, styled bold/italic/code/link runs, task
  checkboxes, block quotes, code cards, and GFM tables into a paginated PDF; `MarkdownOptions.
  FontFamily`/`CodeFontFamily` (or explicit `LoadFont` faces) cover non-Latin text. `SaveMarkdown`/
  `WriteMarkdown` reverse the process, inferring headings from font size and recovering
  bold/italic/code runs, links, and nested lists — tables are not yet reconstructed and flow as
  paragraphs.

facts.value:
- `SearchText` (literal, case-insensitive, or RE2 regex, with an optional region) returns
  per-match bounding boxes built from per-glyph positions; `ReplaceText` redraws the replacement
  at the same baseline/size/colour in a metric-compatible Standard-14 face (or, for text that face
  cannot show, in `ReplaceOptions.Font` or the original's family found by name), and with
  `ReplaceAdjustmentShiftRestOfLine` moves the rest of the line by the change in width so a
  longer replacement does not overlap what follows. `ReplaceOptions.Rectangle` lays the
  replacement out as a paragraph instead — wrapped at whole words, optionally justified
  (`ReplaceAdjustmentAdjustSpaceWidth`), shrunk or scaled to fit (`FontSizeAdjustment`), its
  edges moved with `LeftAdjustment`/`RightAdjustment`. A literal query matches within a line; a
  regular expression also matches across line breaks (and, on a document, across pages), each
  match carrying one segment per line; `SearchForTextRelatedGraphics` also reports the
  colour of the highlight or cell shading each match is drawn over.
  `RemoveAllText` on a page or a document removes every text operator, in Form XObjects too,
  and keeps graphics and images.
- `Document.ExtractImages()`/`Page.ExtractImages()` decode every image on all pages (or one page)
  as JPEG (DCTDecode passthrough) or PNG, across DeviceRGB/DeviceGray/DeviceCMYK/Indexed/ICCBased
  color spaces with soft masks applied as PNG alpha; `Document.ImageInfos()`/`Page.ImageInfos()`
  list the same images' position, size, and color space *without* decoding pixel data, for fast,
  selective extraction (call `.Extract()` on just the ones you need). `AddImage`/
  `AddImageFromStream` (a file path or an `io.Reader`, respectively; an Image XObject either way)
  is the recommended default for anything larger than a tiny icon, where `AddInlineImage` is more
  appropriate.
- `ImageToDocument(path, opts...)`/`ImageToDocumentFromStream(r, opts...)` build a brand-new
  single-page `*Document` from a standalone JPEG or PNG file, with `ImageToDocumentOptions`
  controlling explicit `PageWidth`/`PageHeight` and margins (0 = size the page from the image's
  own DPI). An already-placed page image can be swapped in place with `ImageInfo.Replace(path)`/
  `.ReplaceFromStream(r)` (format auto-detected from magic bytes; position and size on the page
  stay unchanged even if the new image's own dimensions differ) or removed entirely with
  `ImageInfo.Remove()` (deletes the XObject reference and its drawing operators from the page;
  page-level images only, not ones nested inside a Form XObject).

facts.value:
- Viewer permissions (`Permissions`/`SetPermissions`) are enforced by PDF viewers, not by this
  library — the encryption bitfield is written into the file, but the library itself is not a
  DRM mechanism.
- Linearization (`SaveLinearized`/`WriteToLinearized`) cannot be combined with encryption or
  digital signing in the same document.
- Certificate-based encryption accepts RSA recipients only (PKCS#1 v1.5 key transport); elliptic
  curve recipients (key agreement) and the legacy RC4 sub-filters are not written.
- OpenType shaping covers Arabic-family, Hebrew, and simple (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek) scripts; the
  Indic, Khmer, Myanmar, and Hangul reordering shapers and vertical text are not implemented.
- `ConvertToPDFA` embeds a font only when a face is available to it: Symbol and ZapfDingbats need
  one registered through `AddFontFile`/`AddFontFolder` (no metric-compatible clone is bundled),
  and a composite font needs the matching face installed. A font whose licensing bits forbid
  embedding is left alone. Confirm full conformance with a dedicated validator such as veraPDF.
- `ConvertDeviceCMYKToRGB` leaves what it cannot convert in place, and `ValidatePDFA` keeps reporting
  it: mesh shadings holding colours in their data, DeviceN spaces of more than 8 colorants, JPEG
  images with a colour-key mask, and images or functions that cannot be decoded.
- `FlattenTransparency` only looks at a page's content stream and `/Resources` graph; an
  annotation's own opacity or the transparency inside its `/AP` appearance stream is untouched —
  flatten annotations into page content first (`Annotation.Flatten()`/`Form.Flatten()`) if that
  also needs to go. It also only rasterizes whole pages, not just the transparent region within
  one, so a flattened page's text is no longer extractable.
- The built-in renderer does not support mesh shadings (PDF shading types 4-7); other shading
  types, patterns, and blend modes render normally.
- `ConvertToGrayscale` maps device colours, images, and shadings/patterns to their luminance grey
  in place, but Separation/DeviceN, Indexed, and PostScript/sampled shading functions are
  best-effort only.
- `MarkdownToDocument` has no syntax highlighting yet; `SaveMarkdown` does not reconstruct tables
  from a PDF (cell text flows as paragraphs) and caps inferred heading levels at 3.
- A literal `SearchText`/`ReplaceText` query matches within a single text line; use a regular
  expression (`\s+` between words) for one that may straddle a line break. A replacement across
  lines goes on the first line, and the matched text on later lines is removed.
- Scanned pages are auto-detected (no extractable text plus a dominant full-page image);
  `OcrOptions.Pages`/`All` override the default selection when auto-detection guesses wrong. The
  bundled `LLMOCREngine` returns line-level OCR text with no coordinates, so
  `MakeSearchable` positions the hidden searchable text on an even grid rather than exact
  per-word boxes; implement the one-method `ai.OCREngine` interface over an engine that reports
  word boxes (e.g. Tesseract or a cloud OCR service) for exact alignment. For non-Latin text,
  pass a Unicode font via `OcrOptions.Font` (see `Document.LoadFont`).
- The AI copilots (summarization, OCR, chat, alt-text) send extracted document text and/or
  rendered page images to the configured endpoint. For sensitive documents, point the client at a
  local endpoint (e.g. Ollama) — the same client code works unchanged.
- `Table` does not yet support content-driven auto-fit column widths, per-side border dash
  patterns, or a `RowSpan` group splitting across a page break.

attributes.docstring_full: oaMessage carries either a plain string content (text-only message) or an array of content parts (vision).
annotationBase is embedded into every concrete annotation type. It owns the underlying pdfDict and tracks attachment state.

drawingAnnotationBase is the shared embedded base for the four geometric drawing annotation types (Square/Circle/Line/Ink). It provides the BorderStyle/DashPattern/BorderWidth accessors and the regen-aware SetRect/SetColor overrides — all of which are identical across the four drawing types. Concrete types embed drawingAnnotationBase and set the regenerate field in their constructor to a closure that calls the type-specific generator (e.g. setAppearanceN(&a.annotationBase, generateSquareAppearance(a))). Setters on this base call regenerate() after mutating the dict, so /AP/N stays in sync without per-type accessor duplication.

markupAnnotationBase is the shared body of the four text-markup annotations (Highlight, Underline, StrikeOut, Squiggly), which differ only in /Subtype and in how they draw themselves. The quad accessors live here, and — as on drawingAnnotationBase for the shape annotations — every setter that changes what the annotation looks like calls the regenerate hook the concrete type installs, so /AP/N always matches the properties.

polyAnnotationBase is the shared embedded base for the two vertex-based annotation types, Polygon and PolyLine. It provides the /Vertices accessor, /IC interior colour, /Rect recomputation from the vertices, and the BorderWidth override that keeps /Rect in sync — all identical across the two types. The concrete type sets the regenerate closure in its constructor so /AP/N stays current after any mutation. Mirrors the shape shared by Aspose.PDF for .NET's PolygonAnnotation and PolylineAnnotation (both expose Vertices + InteriorColor).
cornerMarkLayout is where a trim or bleed mark goes: lines through (x, y), each starting at (startX, startY) and running length outwards.
cornerPrinterMark is what trim and bleed marks share. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's CornerPrinterMarkAnnotation.
printerMarkBoxes are the page boxes the marks are placed by.
appearanceBuilder accumulates PDF content-stream operators for use as a Form XObject /AP/N body. Operators are emitted in PDF spec form, one per line, separated by newlines.
arabicForms holds the contextual forms of one Arabic letter (0 = the form does not exist for this letter) plus its joining behaviour.
atElem is one structure element being built. Leaves own content (their MCIDs); groups (L, LI, Table, TR) only hold children.
atPageAnalysis turns one page's flow blocks into structure elements.
Phase 1: analyse and rewrite every page in memory.
atAnnot is one annotation of a page on its way into the structure tree.
atItem is one unit of the rewritten stream.
atMC is one open marked-content section of the original stream.
atPiece is one rewritten operator with its owner.
atTok is one element of a text-showing operator: a glyph (its encoded bytes and the page-space point it is tested at) or a TJ kerning number.
Text: group tokens into runs of one owner. A kerning number belongs to the run of the glyph before it (a leading one to the first run).

barcodeModules is a rectangular grid of ink/no-ink barcode modules, row-major top-to-bottom, quiet zone already baked in — the common representation renderBarcodeModules returns regardless of symbology.
qrBitWriter accumulates a sequence of MSB-first bits, later packed into bytes by bytes().

qrMatrix is the working module grid during encoding: bits holds module colour (true = dark), reserved marks cells that are function patterns, separators, format/version info, or the fixed dark module — never touched by data placement or masking.

qrBlockSpec describes how a QR version's data+EC codewords split into blocks (ISO/IEC 18004 Table 9), for error-correction level M only — the only level this encoder writes (see barcode_qr.go). Some versions split data into two groups of differently-sized blocks (g1 = smaller blocks, g2 = larger); versions with only one group leave g2Blocks at 0.
bidiCls is a (reduced) Unicode bidirectional character class.
ccittBits is an MSB-first bit reader over the encoded data.
ccittParams are the relevant /DecodeParms entries.

cffFont is a parsed CFF program able to produce glyph outlines by glyph ID.

attributes.docstring_full: cffWidths holds a Private DICT's defaultWidthX and nominalWidthX (Technical Note #5176, Table 23): a charstring's width is the nominal plus what it states, or the default when it states none.
unicodeMap collects a CMap's destinations: the first character of every code, plus the whole sequence for codes that stand for several characters (a ligature glyph mapped to "fi").

cidCMap maps character codes to CIDs for a composite (Type0) font, per the CMap text format (ISO 32000-1 §9.7.5 / Adobe TN #5099). It handles a variable-width codespace (1–4 bytes), so a single byte string mixes 1-byte Latin codes and 2-byte CJK codes (e.g. GBK-EUC-H). The same parser serves the predefined Adobe CMaps (embedded, gzip'd) and a PDF's own embedded /Encoding CMap stream.

attributes.declaration: type cmykColorState struct{ fill, stroke cmykKind }

attributes.docstring_full: cmykKind says how sc/scn operands relate to the current colour space.

mdLinkRef is a link reference definition ([label]: dest "title").
mdListData describes a list or list-item marker; two markers belong to the same list when Type/Delim/BulletChar match.

mdEmitState carries the serializer's cross-block context: the active list (kind + its base indent, for nesting) and the just-emitted heading (so a heading the extractor split across lines can be merged back).

attributes.declaration: type mdSink func(name, mime string, data []byte) (string, error)
attributes.docstring_full: mdSink turns an image into a referencable URL; nil = skip images.
inlNode is the working doubly-linked node; converted to *mdInline at the end (the linked shape is required by the emphasis/link algorithms, which splice ranges of siblings into new parents).

attributes.declaration: type location struct{ stream, index int }

attributes.docstring_full: packedObj is one object destined for an object stream: its output number and its serialized value, without the "obj"/"endobj" wrapper.

xrefStreamEntry is one row of a cross-reference stream (ISO 32000-1 §7.5.8.3 Table 18): type 0 free (f2 next free object, f3 generation), type 1 in use (f2 byte offset, f3 generation), type 2 compressed (f2 object-stream number, f3 index within it).
ocspCertID names the certificate being asked about, by hashes of its issuer plus its serial (RFC 6960 §4.1.1).
gsubReverseChain is GSUB type 8: one-to-one substitution applied in reverse order with backtrack and lookahead context.
otAnchor is an attachment point in font units. exists distinguishes "at the origin" from "no anchor here" (a NULL offset in the source).
otClassDef assigns each glyph a class number; glyphs not listed are class 0.

otCoverage maps a glyph to its coverage index, or reports absence. Format 1 keeps the sorted glyph list; format 2 keeps ranges. Both are searched by bisection, which is what makes lookup application cheap.

otLayout is a font's parsed layout tables. It hangs off ttfFont, built on the first shaping request and cached (nil when the font has neither GSUB nor GPOS, which is the common case for Latin-only subsets).
otLayoutTable is the common shape of GSUB and GPOS: a script list selecting features, a feature list selecting lookups, and the lookups.
otLookup is one lookup: a type, the flags that decide which glyphs it skips, and its subtables (already resolved through any extension indirection, so kind is the real lookup type).
otMarkRecord is a mark glyph's class plus its attachment anchor.
otSeqRule is one glyph-sequence rule; input excludes the first glyph, which the subtable's coverage already matched.
otValueRecord is a GPOS adjustment in font units. Device-table offsets in the source record are skipped, not applied.
otKernSubtable is the pairs of one format 0 subtable, keyed left<<16|right.

outlineEntry is a flat representation of an outline item used during the write pass. It carries the underlying *OutlineItemCollection plus the wiring (parent/prev/next/first/last) needed to emit a PDF dict.
numberTreeEntry is a single key→dict pair from a PDF number tree.
resizePlan is a page's new MediaBox (unrotated user space, origin 0,0) and the matrix taking the old content there.
columnRegion is a part of a page, top to bottom, with its own columns.

attributes.declaration: type sides struct{ left, right, cross bool }
type ref struct{ page, sec, par int }
attributes.docstring_full: carrier: where the paragraph that may continue lives.
pdfVersion is a PDF version as major*10+minor (14 = PDF 1.4, 20 = PDF 2.0); 0 means unknown.

deviceColorScan looks for the first use of one device colour space in what a page paints: its content, the forms, patterns, shadings, images, soft masks and Type3 glyphs that content reaches, and its annotations' normal appearances.

attributes.declaration: type fontIssue struct{ rule, msg string }
attributes.docstring_full: fontIssue is one violation found in a font, named without a PDF/A or PDF/UA prefix so either validator can report it under its own codes.
glyphFont is what the walk over a document's text collects for one font.
inheritedResources is what one form takes from those drawing it.

attributes.declaration: type resourceUse struct{ category, name string }
attributes.docstring_full: resourceUse is a name a content stream looks up in its resources.
algorithmIdentifier is the X.509 AlgorithmIdentifier. For digest algorithms the parameters are an explicit ASN.1 NULL; for ECDSA they are absent. We model both by making Parameters optional+raw.
attribute is a CMS signed/unsigned attribute (RFC 5652 §5.3).

contentInfo is the outer CMS wrapper (RFC 5652 §3). Content carries its own [0] EXPLICIT tag in the RawValue (a struct tag would be ignored because the value is pre-encoded), so no asn1 struct tag is set.
encapContentInfo carries the content type; for a detached signature the eContent itself is omitted.

essCertIDv2 / signingCertificateV2 implement the ESS signing-certificate-v2 signed attribute (RFC 5035 §5.4), required by PAdES/CAdES. The hash algorithm defaults to SHA-256, so it is omitted and only the cert hash is carried.
issuerAndSerial identifies the signer's certificate (RFC 5652 §5.3).
signedData is the CMS SignedData (RFC 5652 §5.1).
signerInfo is one CMS SignerInfo (RFC 5652 §5.3). SignedAttrs / UnsignedAttrs already carry their own [0]/[1] IMPLICIT tags in FullBytes, so no struct tag is set; UnsignedAttrs is omitted when empty.
messageImprint and timeStampReq model the RFC 3161 TimeStampReq.

parsedSignedData mirrors the SignedData SEQUENCE for unmarshaling. The IMPLICIT-tagged fields are captured as raw values and descended into by hand, which is more robust than relying on asn1 struct tags for the IMPLICIT SET OF forms.
encryptedContentInfo is RFC 5652 §6.1. The content is carried inline as an implicitly tagged [0] OCTET STRING.
envelopedDataASN is RFC 5652 §6.1 with the optional originatorInfo and unprotectedAttrs omitted (version 0).
ktRecipientInfo is a CMS KeyTransRecipientInfo (RFC 5652 §6.2.1) using the issuerAndSerialNumber choice, which is what PDF producers emit.
fillRule selects the winding rule used to decide which regions of a path are inside.

rasterizer turns flattened device-space paths into per-pixel coverage in [0,1]. It uses analytic coverage along X and supersampling along Y, which gives smooth anti-aliasing with a small, predictable amount of work and no dependencies.
devPath is a path flattened to straight segments in device space.
flattener builds a devPath from move/line/curve calls, adaptively subdividing Bézier curves until they are within tol device units of straight segments.

attributes.declaration: type point struct{ x, y float64 }
attributes.docstring_full: point is a device-space coordinate (pixels, Y-down).

subpath is a flattened polyline. For filling it is treated as implicitly closed (the rasterizer connects the last point back to the first); the closed flag records whether the source path explicitly closed it (used by stroking).
strokeStyle carries the stroke parameters the rasterizing stroker honors: half line width, line cap, line join, and miter limit (ISO 32000-1 §8.4.3).
doAction is the classification result for a single Do operator.
doActionKind categorises what to do with a Do operator.

formCloneKey identifies one Form XObject placement's redacted output uniquely enough to memoize it (pdf-go-wuv7): redactFormXObject's output depends only on the source stream, the CTM in effect (composed with the form's own /Matrix, which is intrinsic to form and so need not be included separately), the redaction regions (constant within one page — collected once in applyRedactionsToPage — so not part of the key), and the inherited text state seeding its nested text rewrite, if any. Two placements agreeing on all of these produce byte-identical redacted content. form is compared by pointer identity, which correctly distinguishes different source objects — resolveRef always returns the same *pdfStream for the same object number within one Document, and nothing in this redaction pass ever mutates an original (unredacted) form's stream value in place (clone-not-mutate throughout).

formRedactBudget is a work counter, shared (by pointer) across every level of Form XObject recursion within the ONE page it was constructed for — see maxFormRedactWork for why the scope is per-page, not per-ApplyRedactions-call. It also memoizes clones (pdf-go-wuv7) and remembers the next free "/FmN" resource index, both for the same reason: every level of recursion, and both callers that create clones (redactFormDo for page content, redactOneAnnotationAppearance for annotation appearances), share this one instance per page.
patternColourState is the part of the graphics state this scan tracks: the pattern name selected as the fill / stroke colour, or "" when the current colour is not a pattern.

cidGlyph is one decoded Type0 glyph in a Tj/TJ string: raw is the exact content-stream bytes this glyph's code occupied (2 bytes for Identity-H/V, 1-4 for a font with its own CMap — pdf-go-eys1), kept verbatim so a surviving glyph's bytes are re-emitted unchanged.

fontInterner hands out one shared *fontInfo per font resource name, so a content-stream walker and every q/Q snapshot it takes point at the same fontInfo rather than each holding a ~3 KB copy. Scoped to one font map: a walker whose map changes (a Form XObject with its own /Resources) uses a fresh interner for it.
glyphFilterState holds the current text rendering state for glyph filtering.

mcSpan tracks one open BDC/BMC marked-content span while this function walks a content stream, for the /ActualText scrub (pdf-go-1ha8): outIdx is where its BDC/BMC op landed in out (so EMC can replace it in place once it knows whether anything inside was dropped), tagOperand is the BDC's original tag operand (reused verbatim if the op is rewritten), props is a PRIVATE, owned copy of its resolved properties dict (nil if it has none, or none could be resolved — e.g. a /Properties name with no resources to resolve it against), and dropped records whether any glyph drawn anywhere inside this span (at any nesting depth beneath it) was redacted.

textGState is the subset of this walker's running state that "q" saves and "Q" restores — the graphics-state (not text-object-state) parameters of ISO 32000-1 Table 52, the same fields textExtractor's own gsStack (text.go) saves/restores. font is a pointer into a shared, never-mutated fontInfo (see fontInterner), not a copy: a fontInfo is ~3 KB (two 256-entry arrays), so snapshotting it by value let a flood of unmatched "q" operators — two bytes each, highly compressible — cost ~3 KB of live memory apiece and ~17 KB of allocation once the stack's growth copies are counted (pdf-go-ifpy point 3; ~900 bytes per q now). text.go's extractorGState had the identical pattern and holds a pointer too.
formKey names a form and, for one with no /Resources of its own, the resources its names resolve through (they decide what it draws).
formResult is a stripped form: its clone (0 when it holds no text) and the redirections it passes up to its caller's resources.
gstate is the subset of the PDF graphics state the renderer tracks.
renderer interprets a page's content stream and paints onto img.

attributes.declaration: type blendFunc func(cb, cs float64) float64
attributes.docstring_full: blendFunc is a separable blend mode B(Cb, Cs): given a backdrop and source channel value in [0,1] it returns the blended channel (ISO 32000-1 §11.3.5). A nil blendFunc means Normal (plain source-over).

blendMode is the active blend on the graphics state: at most one of sep / ns is non-nil; the zero value is Normal (plain source-over). css carries the CSS mix-blend-mode keyword for the SVG export ("" = normal).

attributes.declaration: type nonSepBlend func(cbr, cbg, cbb, csr, csg, csb float64) (float64, float64, float64)
attributes.docstring_full: nonSepBlend is a non-separable blend mode operating on the whole colour (ISO 32000-1 §11.3.5.3): Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity.
tintFunc converts a set of tint values to an 8-bit RGB colour.
fontRef points at one sub-font within a font file (index 0 for a plain .ttf).

FontRepository resolves fonts for rendering from caller-registered folders and files, and optionally the operating system's font directories. It lets a document render Standard-14 (and other non-embedded) text with exact fonts instead of the bundled metric-compatible substitutes. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's FontRepository / FontRepository.Sources. Use the package-level AddFontFolder / AddFontFile / AddSystemFonts. The registry is process-global (fonts are a machine resource) and indexed lazily on first use. Only TrueType (.ttf) outline fonts are used by the renderer.

fnPostScript is a Type 4 (PostScript calculator) function (ISO 32000-1 §7.10.5) — a small stack-based program mapping m inputs to n outputs. These are the common tint transforms for Separation/DeviceN colour and some shadings.
psItem is one program element: a number (float64), an operator (string), or a nested procedure ([]psItem, consumed by if/ifelse).
glyphPoint is a control point of a glyph outline in font design units, with on/off-curve flag (TrueType quadratic outlines).
fnConst is the fallback for an unparseable function: a constant value.

fnParser parses one function tree. A function object reached again is the one already parsed: a stitching function whose /Functions name the same object several times, level after level, would otherwise be parsed once per path, which grows exponentially with the depth. One that refers back to itself, or nests deeper than maxFunctionDepth, is a constant.

pdfFunc evaluates a PDF function: it maps m input values to n output components (ISO 32000-1 §7.10). Most types here are 1-input (shadings, Separation); only the PostScript calculator (type 4) is genuinely multi-input (DeviceN tint transforms).

renderFont carries what the renderer needs to draw glyphs of one font: the TrueType program (outlines), CID→GID mapping, and per-code advance widths. Only embedded TrueType (Type0/CIDFontType2 with /FontFile2, and simple /TrueType) fonts are renderable here; Standard-14 outlines arrive in P4.
textState holds the PDF text-object state used while rendering.

attributes.declaration: type tileIJ struct{ i, j int }

attributes.docstring_full: tilingPattern is a parsed PatternType 1 pattern: a content stream (the cell) tiled across an area by /XStep and /YStep, mapped through /Matrix. PaintType 1 patterns carry their own colour; PaintType 2 (uncolored) inherit the current fill colour, captured in the graphics state when the pattern was selected.
lineShift moves text on one line: glyphs whose baseline is within tol of y and that start at or after fromX move by dx along the line.
replaceFonts picks the font each replacement is drawn in (ReplaceOptions.Font) and keeps the faces loaded by name, so each is embedded once per call.
replaceMatch is a located match plus the appearance needed to redraw it.
paragraphLine is one wrapped line of a paragraph replacement; last marks the last line of a paragraph of the replacement (before a "\n" or at its end), which justification leaves as it is.

replaceLayout is how ReplaceText lays a replacement out as a paragraph in a rectangle (pdf-go-2tdw): ReplaceOptions.Rectangle, FontSizeAdjustment, LeftAdjustment/RightAdjustment and the paragraph adjustments.
httpRevocationFetcher is the built-in transport.
otFeatSpec is one entry of a feature plan: the feature tag and the glyph mask that gates it.
otMatcher decides which glyphs a lookup steps over. LookupFlag says to ignore whole GDEF classes, or to accept only marks of one attachment class or mark-glyph set.
otPlanLookup is a lookup selected by the plan, with the union of the masks of the features that referenced it.
otShaper holds the state of one shaping run.
shapedGlyph is one output glyph in font units.

callbackSigner adapts a SignHash callback to crypto.Signer, so a remote signing service travels the same path as a local key. Public() answers from the certificate, which is the only public key a verifier will use anyway.
--- Collect everything to emit (new objects + modified existing). ---
xrefRow is one entry to write into the incremental xref table.

stampBase holds the placement and appearance common to every stamp. Its exported fields mirror the corresponding Aspose.Pdf.Stamp properties (HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment, Opacity, RotateAngle, Background).
svgClipPath defines a clipping path; referenced by shapes via clip-path="url(#id)".
svgGradient is the interface for both linear and radial gradients.
svgGradientStop is one stop in a gradient (offset 0..1, resolved color, opacity 0..1).
svgPaint is a tagged union for fill/stroke values: solid color OR gradient ref. Both fields nil/empty means "none"/"transparent" (the caller should treat as no paint).
svgImage is the IR node for an SVG element.

svgMask defines a mask; referenced by shapes via mask="url(#id)". maskUnits determines the coordinate system for the mask container (default: objectBoundingBox). maskContentUnits determines the coordinate system for children (default: userSpaceOnUse).

gradAxis distinguishes gradient coordinates by how percent units resolve against the viewport when gradientUnits is userSpaceOnUse: x-axis coords (cx, fx, x1, x2) scale by viewport width y-axis coords (cy, fy, y1, y2) scale by viewport height radius scales by sqrt((vw² + vh²) / 2) per SVG 1.1 §7.10

gradCoord holds a parsed gradient coordinate before it is resolved against the gradient's coordinate system. value is already 0..1 when isPct is true (parseSVGGradientLength normalises percent to fraction).
textCursor tracks the current text insertion position shared across all runs within a element (including nested s).
svgText is the IR node for an SVG element.
svgTextRun is a single contiguous text run at an absolute position. One element produces one or more runs (one per + leading/trailing CharData of the parent text element).
svgNode is the interface implemented by every IR node.
svgPathOp is one normalized path command (absolute coords, expanded shortcut).

svgPreserveAspect holds the parsed preserveAspectRatio attribute. align is one of "none" / "xMinYMin" / "xMidYMin" / "xMaxYMin" / "xMinYMid" / "xMidYMid" / "xMaxYMid" / "xMinYMax" / "xMidYMax" / "xMaxYMax". meetOrSlice is "meet" (default) or "slice"; ignored when align == "none".
svgStyle holds resolved presentation attributes after parent cascade.
svgViewBox holds the four numbers of .
svgSymbol is a container with its own viewBox. Not rendered directly; only referenced via .
svgUse is a placeholder before resolveUseReferences (Task 6) replaces it with the cloned referent. After resolution, no *svgUse nodes remain in the IR tree.
framedFragment is a fragment with its position in its own text direction: x along the baseline, y across it, so rotated text orders into lines as horizontal text does.
latticeCell is one physical (possibly spanning) ruled cell.
latticeIntersections returns the grid points where an H and a V rule cross (within tolerance), plus fast lookup structures.

quarterFrame maps page space to the frame of text rotated by rot (90 or 270 degrees) on a page w by h, and back. Both frames keep coordinates positive so the column histogram of the prose guard sees them.
pathPaint describes how a visited path was painted.
pathSeg is one straight segment of a visited path, in page space.
pathVisit is one painted path delivered to the visitPaths callback.
rule is one canonical ruling line. For horizontal rules pos = Y and lo/hi span X; vertical rules mirror.
shadedRect is a larger filled rectangle (cell shading) with its colour.
streamCellSpan is one gap-delimited fragment group within a line.
streamRow is one candidate table row.
edgeKey identifies a drawn border-line segment by its rounded coordinates (×1000, rounded). Two cells sharing an edge produce identical keys after normalizing endpoint order.
edgeSet tracks edges already emitted on the current page. A nil edgeSet disables dedup (legacy behavior).
edgeStyle is the visual style of a border edge — width + stroke RGB. Two edges with the same coordinates but different style render both (caller intent preserved).
spanGroup is a contiguous range of rows that must be drawn together (no page break inside). [start, end] are inclusive row indices.

tableTagger drives structure-tree tagging while a table is rendered: it owns the /Table element and creates a /TR per row and a /TH/TD per cell as cells are drawn. Header rows (the table's repeating rows) become /TH.

extractorGState is the slice of state that q/Q save and restore. Per ISO 32000-1 Table 52 the text-state parameters (font, size, char/word spacing, leading, horizontal scaling) and the fill colour are part of the graphics state, so q/Q must roll them back along with the CTM. The text matrices (tm/lm) are text-object state, not graphics state, so they are NOT saved here — a q/Q may nest inside a BT/ET block. Without restoring the font, text drawn after a "q … /Fsub Tf … Q" block kept the inner font and decoded through the wrong encoding (Binder1.pdf: TOTAL rows became "3?3>;").
markedContentEntry tracks a BDC/BMC nesting level. When actualText is non-nil, glyphs inside are suppressed and the pointed-to string is emitted instead when the matching EMC is encountered.
textFragment is a contiguous run of text at a single position.

textRunState is the part of the text state a found fragment reports and extraction itself does not use: word spacing (Tw), horizontal scaling (Tz, percent), the rendering mode (Tr) and the stroking colour.
encodeFn returns a PDF string operand for s — "(...)" for single-byte encoding, " " for hex glyph IDs.

attributes.declaration: type fontResolver func(font Font, resources pdfDict) (resName string, width widthFn, encode encodeFn, ascent, descent float64, err error)
attributes.docstring_full: fontResolver registers a font into the caller's /Resources dict (when resources is non-nil) and returns the local resource name (e.g. "/F1") plus per-font callbacks. Page.AddText supplies a page-level resolver that delegates to p.ensureStandardFontResource / p.ensureEmbeddedFontResource; FreeText/Stamp /AP rendering will supply an XObject-level resolver in later tasks.

lineMeasurer measures candidate text for word-wrap decisions so they agree with what will actually be drawn (GitHub issue #14: AddText used to wrap by the unshaped per-rune sum even for a font that OpenType-shapes — kerning/ligatures then make the drawn line narrower or wider than the width used to wrap it, causing an early wrap or a clipped overflow). For an unshaped font (no GSUB/GPOS, or Standard-14/Type3 — shaper is nil) word/space/exact are all the plain per-rune advance sum: that is also exactly what gets drawn, so the wrapping decision is already exact and output stays byte-identical to before shaping existed. For a font that shapes (fontHasShaping), word/space are a FAST estimate — each word (or a single space) shaped on its own and cached, which is exact for everything shaping does WITHIN a word (ligatures, contextual forms, intra-word kerning — joining never crosses a space) but can miss kerning BETWEEN two glyphs either side of the inter-word space, which a font rarely defines. exact always re-shapes the whole candidate exactly as renderTextInBuilder's draw loop will, so a caller can verify a greedily-packed line before committing to it and back a word off (into the next line) on the rare mismatch — see wrapText/nextLine. This keeps the common case cheap (one shape call per word, cached; one exact reshape per finished line, not per word added to it) instead of reshaping a growing candidate line from scratch for every word. A second, narrower gap (code review of this fix, unconfirmed against a real font): shaping a word alone picks its OpenType script from that word's own characters (otScriptTag), which could in principle disagree with the script the real line-level shape applies to the SAME characters, if the word's bidi embedding level in context splits it across a run boundary that shaping it alone does not see. The direction that matters is an OVERestimate from this: exact's backoff corrects an UNDERestimate just fine (a line it let overflow still gets re-measured and popped back correctly, since exact always uses the real baseLevel/bidi), but it has no way to ADD a word back that the greedy pack, discouraged by an inflated word() estimate, never tried to fit in the first place — so the only possible symptom is a wrap one word earlier than strictly necessary, never an overflow. Whether this is reachable at all is not established.
Track positions for underline/strikethrough.
widthFn returns advance width in points for a single rune.

singleLineShape carries whatever a single already-finished line needs for measuring/drawing without any word-wrapping: either a shapedLine (for a font with OpenType GSUB/GPOS tables) or the plain, possibly bidi-reordered, text plus a widthFn. Shared by AddTextAt and MeasureText so both apply the exact same Arabic-shaping/bidi/OpenType-shaping pipeline renderTextInBuilder's per-line draw step does for one already- wrapped line (GitHub issue #18) — the only piece deliberately left out here is wrapText itself.
textEditPlan is one changed fragment: what to remove and what to draw.
textEditTx remembers what drawing changes on the pages an edit touches, so a failure part way through leaves the document as it was.
fragmentBinding ties a fragment to the page it was drawn on or found on, with a snapshot of how it looked then, so later edits can be detected.

fragmentSnapshot records a fragment's text, position, own state and each segment's state (resolved for authored fragments, as found for found ones). Colours are copied by value, fonts kept by identity.
ownedPiece is what a drawn segment drew besides its glyphs: its background box (the id of its marked-content section, 0 for none) and its link.
documentFont is a font found on a page: its name as text extraction reports it. Usable as TextState.Font for reading; drawing with it goes through the replacement fallback.

pageFont is a font already on a page, drawn with again when an edit of found text needs no other glyphs (pdf-go-ddpy): a change of colour, background, underline, size or, emulated, style redraws the text in the document's own font, so it keeps its shapes and widths instead of moving to a Standard-14 substitute of another width. It encodes a character with the code the font already shows it with and measures it with the font's own widths. Only simple fonts (not Type3) and composite fonts with Identity-H or a horizontal CMap are used this way. For a font with an embedded program, only characters the edited fragment already showed in it count as covered: a subset need not hold the others.
paraLine is one laid-out line of the paragraph.
paraPiece is a part of a line drawn on its own: a segment, or one word.
paraRun is one segment of a paragraph line, resolved.
paraTextLine is a line of an AbsorbedTextParagraph: its baseline, size and words, left to right.

lineRuneMap flattens a line's fragments into one rune stream, recording for each rune its byte offset, owning fragment index (-1 for an inserted inter-fragment space), and rune index within that fragment. Shared by text search (searchLine) and text replace (collectReplaceMatchesLine).
lineSpan is the part of a match on one line: runes [r0, r1) of the line's rune map.
pageLines is a page's layout lines.
spanMatch is a match found across lines: its text and its part on each line it covers.
bidiRun is a maximal stretch of a line at one embedding level, in logical order.
shapedLine is one line shaped into positioned glyphs, in drawing order.
tocItem is an internal TOC line with a stable target reference (the underlying page object) so a page number can be resolved after pages are inserted ahead of the target.
tocOpts is the resolved (defaulted) form of TOCOptions.
tableRecord is an entry in the TTF table directory.
ttfFont holds the parsed fields required for PDF embedding and text measurement.

type1Font is a parsed embedded Type1 (PostScript) font program — the /FontFile form, as opposed to TrueType (/FontFile2) or CFF (/FontFile3). Its glyph outlines come from eexec-encrypted Type1 charstrings keyed by glyph name; a synthetic GID is assigned to each name so the renderer's GID-based glyph path can drive it.
t1Interp is the Type1 charstring interpreter state.
pdfDict is a PDF dictionary.
pdfDirectRef is like pdfRef but writeValue outputs it without remapping. Use this when the object number is already in the output (new) space.
pdfName is a PDF name object like /Name.
pdfNull represents PDF null.
pdfObject is an indirect object "n g obj ... endobj".
pdfRef is an indirect reference "n g R".
pdfStream is a PDF stream object.
xrefEntry describes where to find a PDF object.
pageInfo describes a single PDF page reached while walking the page tree.
rawDocument is a parsed PDF used internally by Validate and the password-aware Open path. It is distinct from the public Document type.
pathOp is a single operation in a Path. Unused fields for the kind are zero.
pathOpKind enumerates the kinds of operations a Path can contain.
xlsxCell is one resolved cell ready for serialization.
xlsxDrawEntry is one image anchored on a worksheet.
xlsxMedia is one image payload destined for xl/media.
xlsxSheet is one worksheet: sparse rows of cells plus column widths.
xlsxStyle is a deduplicable cell look. Zero value = default style (index 0).
xlsxStyleRegistry interns styles into cellXfs indexes.
Vertical bands: every table is one band; every non-table line is its own band, ordered by Y descending.
xrefTable holds all cross-reference entries for a document.

attributes.docstring_full: TestXFormCanvasAddImageAfterFreezeDoesNotMutateResources is the internal-package companion to TestXFormCanvasAddImageAfterFreezeErrors (canvas_frozen_test.go): it directly inspects the already-built form's /Resources dict — which is the literal same pdfDict Go map as the canvas's own /Resources (makeFormXObjectWithResources stores it by reference, not by copy) — before and after a rejected post-freeze AddImageFromStream call. This property is NOT observable through RemoveUnusedObjects: unlike the orphaned-but-unreachable content-stream objects point 1 of pdf-go-nvpo is about, an image registered into that SHARED resources dict is genuinely reachable from the page (page -> Resources/XObject/ -> form -> its own Resources/XObject/ ), so it is never flagged as unused even though nothing ever draws it — it is pointless, not unreachable. The only way to confirm addImageFromBytes's own checkCanvasNotFrozen guard (image_add.go) is doing its job — rejecting the draw BEFORE the image object is created and wired into that shared dict, not merely failing later at the content-stream append the way every other draw primitive does — is to check the dict's own entries directly.

attributes.docstring_full: TestFlattenTransparencyPreservesRotation guards renderContentForFlatten's deliberate choice to rasterize in the page's own unrotated coordinate space rather than the rotated space RenderImage normally produces (see flatten_transparency.go): a rotated page's replacement image must render the same way as the same page rotated but never flattened, not double-rotated or un-rotated. Previously verified only by an ad hoc visual check outside the test suite; this pins it down as an automated regression test. The comparison is a small-tolerance byte diff, not exact equality: deviceMatrix rounds the embed-time pixel dimensions (roundPx) and the image is then rescaled to the box's exact point dimensions on redisplay, so a few tenths of a percent of bytes legitimately differ at content edges from ordinary sub-pixel resampling — the same thing any rasterize-then-redisplay pipeline does, not a defect. A real double-rotation/flip/translation bug differs everywhere (empirically >50% of bytes for this fixture), nowhere close to the threshold below.

attributes.docstring_full: TestApplyRedactionsFormXObjectExhaustedWorkBudgetRefuses is the integration-level counterpart: a form tree shaped to exceed maxFormRedactWork via wide fan-out. attributes.docstring_full: TestApplyRedactionsRemovesFullyCoveredImageBytes pins pdf-go-ye1z: an Image XObject whose placement falls entirely inside a redaction region has its Do invocation dropped from the content stream (rewriteXObjectDoOperatorsInStream's dropDo path), but until this was verified, the page's /Resources/XObject entry for that image was never confirmed to actually go away -- it stayed graph-reachable (page -> Resources -> XObject -> image stream) and RemoveUnusedObjects' ordinary reachability walk would never collect it, so the image's pixel data survived in the saved file even though nothing in the content stream invokes it any more. In practice this already closes on its own: rewriteXObjectDoOperatorsInStream's resource-pruning pass (neededXObjectNames, added for the unrelated pdf-go-w5hl Form-XObject fix) computes which /XObject names the FINAL rewritten content still invokes via ANY Do operator -- Image or Form alike, it does not distinguish -- and deletes every other name from the page's own (already-privatized) /Resources/XObject dict. A dropped Image Do leaves no surviving Do for that name, so it is pruned the same way a redirected Form XObject's now-stale original name is; once pruned, ApplyRedactions' own trailing RemoveUnusedObjects call reclaims the now cleanly-unreachable image stream object. attributes.docstring_full: TestApplyRedactionsDropsInlineImageInRegion pins the inline-image half of pdf-go-xp2u: a BI...ID...EI inline image (ISO 32000-1 §8.9.7) placed entirely inside a redaction region used to fall through rewriteXObjectDoOperatorsInStream's switch into its default case (pass through unchanged) -- the "Do" case only ever looked at Image/Form XObjects, never an inline image, even though both paint into the same unit square under the current CTM. The tombstone+defer rewrite never shifts s.glyphs mid-scan, so it has no such blind spot: every original position is visited exactly once regardless of how many of its neighbors were also tombstoned, so a run of N deletion triggers now removes all N instead of only every other one.
