attributes.docstring: Optimize reduces the document's size in place per opts and returns a report of what changed.
attributes.docstring_full: Optimize reduces the document's size in place per opts and returns a report of what changed. Call before Save/WriteTo. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's Document.OptimizeResources(OptimizationOptions). Order: remove unused objects (a pre-pass, see below) → images → fonts (unembed, then subset what's left embedded) → compress streams → dedupe streams → remove unused objects again (so anything a transform orphans is reclaimed last). RemovedObjects reports the sum of both passes. The pre-pass was added because every (*Page).AddText call (and every table cell) used to replace a page's /Contents with a brand-new stream object holding the whole concatenated content, leaving the old one dead in d.objects with nothing referencing it any more — on a page built from many small AddText calls this meant many dead copies piling up, which RemoveDuplicateStreams and CompressStreams would otherwise both walk and hash/compress for nothing before the final pass cleared them away; on a 20-page, 200-calls-per-page document this made Optimize ~25x slower for no change in the end result. Reported with a clear reproduction and a correct diagnosis by Kare-ino (GitHub issue #9) — thank you. That root cause is now closed at the source (appendToContentStream/prependToContentStream, content_append.go, pdf-go-jbiu/GitHub issue #16: an append now adds one array entry to /Contents instead of rewriting a combined stream, so nothing is ever abandoned), so a document built with the current code produces no such copies in the first place — TestOptimizeManyAddTextCallsStaysFast still pins the speed guarantee itself, now trivially satisfied rather than needing the pre-pass's help. The pre-pass is kept anyway as cheap, harmless insurance against OTHER sources of dead objects this method doesn't know about: a third-party file opened with its own pre-existing orphaned content, or this library's own full-content-replace call sites (ApplyRedactions, ConvertToGrayscale, ImageInfo.Remove, FlattenTransparency — all via replacePageContents or an equivalent, which still swap in one new stream and abandon whatever /Contents pointed at before). Running the same removal once at the very start changes nothing about which objects survive Optimize overall, only when the already-dead ones are noticed, since nothing later in this method can make a genuinely unreachable object reachable again.

It is a read-only diagnostic — it never mutates the document; use ConvertToPDFA to produce a conformant file. Checks performed (ISO 19005-1/2/3, basic level): an XMP metadata packet with a matching pdfaid:part/conformance; every font embedded (no Standard-14 reliance); no encryption; no JavaScript or Launch actions; an ICC OutputIntent when device colours are used; no transparency for PDF/A-1; annotation flags (Print set, Hidden/NoView clear) and appearance streams; an uncompressed /Metadata stream; no LZWDecode (PDF/A-1); no embedded files for PDF/A-1; and what the embedded font programs say about the glyphs drawn (pdfa_glyphs.go); and for PDF/A-4 what ISO 19005-4 asks of /Info, actions and attachments (pdfa4.go). These do not cover every rule of the standards: veraPDF has the last word. Scope: the "a" (tagged/accessible) levels are not validated. This mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's Document.Validate(PdfFormat) but returns a structured report instead of writing an XML log.

attributes.docstring: OpenWithPassword opens a password-protected PDF file.
attributes.docstring_full: OpenWithPassword opens a password-protected PDF file. Use Open for unencrypted files. The password is tried as both user and owner password; either unlocks the document for editing. Returns ErrInvalidPassword if it matches neither. Edit-in-place: the original /O, /U, /P, and /ID bytes from the file are preserved on the returned Document so a subsequent Save reuses them verbatim — BOTH the original user and owner passwords continue to work after re-save, and permissions are preserved bit-for-bit. If you call SetPassword, SetPermissions, SetEncryption, or RemoveEncryption after open, the preserved state is discarded and the document is re-encrypted from the new configuration. Example: doc, err := asposepdf.OpenWithPassword("locked.pdf", "secret")

attributes.docstring: ReplaceText replaces every occurrence of old with replacement on the page and returns the number of replacements made.
attributes.docstring_full: ReplaceText replaces every occurrence of old with replacement on the page and returns the number of replacements made. The matched glyphs are removed and the replacement is drawn at the same baseline, size, and colour in a metric-compatible Standard-14 face chosen from the original's family and style (so it renders even when the original used an embedded subset font that lacks the new glyphs). A replacement that face cannot show, such as Cyrillic or Arabic, is drawn in ReplaceOptions.Font, else in the original's family found by name (see ReplaceOptions.Font); with neither the call fails and nothing is changed. The replacement is shaped and, when right-to-left, ends where the match ended. By default the line is not re-flowed: a much longer replacement may overrun following content; with ReplaceOptions.Adjustment = ReplaceAdjustmentShiftRestOfLine the text after each replacement on its line moves by the difference in width instead (the paragraph is not re-wrapped, so a line can run past its margin); with ReplaceOptions.Rectangle (or the other paragraph options) the replacement is laid out as a wrapped paragraph instead. Matches are located within a single line, like SearchText. Mirrors the find-and-replace idiom of Aspose.PDF for .NET's TextFragmentAbsorber + TextFragment.Text. Text drawn inside a Form XObject is replaced as well: the form is copied for this page with only the matched glyphs removed (its images and paths stay), so other placements of the same form are left unchanged. The ShiftRestOfLine adjustment moves page-level text only. Removing the old text reuses the SAME content-stream rewriter ApplyRedactions does (rewriteTextOperatorsInStream), so it shares that function's one hard limit: a match drawn with a font this pipeline cannot resolve (an undeclared font name, or a simple font with no usable /Encoding/ToUnicode) makes this call return an error instead of replacing it — rather than, as before, silently leaving the OLD text underneath the new replacement text it still drew on top (a real, if cosmetic, bug this change trades for a clear error; found during an independent review of pdf-go-oq9i, the ApplyRedactions fix this inherited). Also removes the dead, now-unreferenced ORIGINAL content stream from the document once at least one match was replaced (RemoveUnusedObjects, the same reason ApplyRedactions calls it — pdf-go-2qkq's class of leak otherwise applies here too, since old text containing whatever was just "replaced" would stay recoverable in the saved file) — so, like ApplyRedactions, call ReplaceText only after placing everything else you mean to keep.
